text:
[LTAC.3.2] The timer fact's schema is named
`$Timer_<rule>_<key>`, where `<rule>` is the parent rule's name
and `<key>` is the clause's key path: the source-order index for a
top-level `after`, and `<outer>_<inner>` for one nested inside
another ([LTAC.6.2.2]). The schema carries two slots, in this order:
`fire_at`, a `Duration`, and `corr`, a `String`.

`fire_at` is the monotonic-clock reading ([LTIM.2.8.2]) at or after
which the follow-up rule may fire. It is a `Duration` because
`monotonic_ns()` returns one ([LTIM.2.2.1]) and the follow-up's guard
compares against it. An `after` delay is relative time, so it runs on
the monotonic clock: a change to the wall clock neither hastens nor
delays it.

`corr` carries the supersedure key from the clause's `as <expr>`
([LRST.1.1]), and is empty when the clause declares none.

The schema declares no `scope` and no `key` / `mutable` markers
because neither applies: the timer fact's lifecycle is explicit —
the follow-up rule retracts it — so it is not a `logical` schema,
and [LFAC.1.7.1]'s declare-every-slot requirement is scoped to
those. An author cannot write this schema in any case.

idris.name: ltac_3_2__capture_timer
idris.note: A TIMER FACT ON THE IDRIS MODEL'S ENGINE: kind 0 in the witnesses' kind order, key 1 (the empty tuple's code), its payload the captured values coded, or 1 for a body that reads nothing. LESS than the clause: no `fire_at` slot -- the entry stamp is `fire_at` less the duration, the module's reading -- and no `corr`, no `as` key being lowered.
